title: refactor: one thin model status proxy at /models/status
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to the model status review: keep only what consumers use.

- Moves the health feed to `GET /models/status` (outside `/v1`) as a raw pass-through of the public Tinybird `model_route_health` pipe, cached 60 s at the edge via `cf.cacheTtl`; deletes the in-memory cache, retries and reshaping (~230 lines → ~60)
- Removes `?status=`, the `Pollinations-Model-Status` header and the `health` field from all model lists; like OpenRouter, `/models` carries no health
- Deletes `shared/registry/model-health.ts`; adds `shared/model-health.ts`, one client-side status helper shared by the website uptime dots and the enter dashboard (previously two copies with different thresholds)
- Enter dashboard fetches `/models/status?minutes=1440` alongside the catalog; website, model monitor, polli-cli and MCP `getModelStatus` point at the new path
- Pipe clamps `minutes` to 1..10080 (staging deployment 148, prod deploy pending)

Why the proxy stays: Tinybird runs the query on every call (24 h window reads ~38 MB in ~0.5 s) and has no result cache, so the edge cache is the only thing keeping browser traffic from hitting it directly.

Breaking: `/v1/models/status` → `/models/status`; `?status=all` health objects gone. Quest #15017 text needs updating after the production deploy.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: One status pipe, no pollen
gist.blurb: Model uptime now travels through one thin, edge-cached pipe instead of a small thicket of reshaping and duplicate helpers. The catalog stays a catalog; status gets its own tidy doorstep.
gist.summary: Moved model health to a raw, 60-second edge-cached GET /models/status proxy for Tinybird’s model_route_health pipe, removed health data and ?status= from /models, and consolidated website and Enter dashboard uptime logic into shared/model-health.ts.
gist.impact: Developers and built-in clients now use /models/status?minutes=1440 (with minutes clamped to 1–10080), while model catalogs stay lighter and browser status checks avoid repeatedly running Tinybird’s 24-hour query.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden observatory represents the newly separated model-status feed: Polli tends a single clear lime-green status pipe leading from a tiny data greenhouse to a retro monitor, while a neat model catalog book sits separately without health badges. The monitor robot can happily inspect the unified uptime dots, with code-plants and flowers showing that one shared helper now feeds both the website and Enter dashboard.
